topics.title: Canvas: Drawing with JavaScript
topics.summary: The canvas element gives a pixel surface you draw on with the 2D context API.
topics.description:
`<canvas>` is a rectangular **bitmap** area that you paint with JavaScript. It is used for games, charts, image editing, particle effects and animations.

```html
<canvas id="c" width="300" height="150">Your browser does not support canvas.</canvas>
```

### Getting a context
```js
const canvas = document.getElementById('c');
const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
```
Other contexts: `webgl`/`webgl2` (3D), `bitmaprenderer`, `webgpu`.

### Basic drawing API
| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `fillStyle` / `strokeStyle` | Colour |
| `fillRect(x,y,w,h)` | Filled rectangle |
| `strokeRect`, `clearRect` | Outline / erase |
| `beginPath()`, `moveTo`, `lineTo`, `arc` | Paths |
| `fill()` / `stroke()` | Paint the path |
| `fillText(text,x,y)` | Text |
| `drawImage(img,x,y)` | Images |

Coordinates start at the **top-left** (0,0); x goes right, y goes **down**.

### Size
Set `width`/`height` **attributes** (the drawing buffer). CSS size only stretches the bitmap and makes it blurry.

### Animation
Use `requestAnimationFrame(loop)`: clear, update, redraw, repeat.

### Canvas vs SVG
Canvas is **pixels** (fast for thousands of objects, no DOM per shape, not accessible by default). SVG is **vectors** (scalable, each shape is a DOM node, stylable). For accessibility provide fallback text or ARIA on the canvas.
keyPoints: canvas is a bitmap drawn through getContext("2d").
Set size with width/height attributes, not CSS.
Origin (0,0) is the top-left corner.
Animate with requestAnimationFrame.
Canvas content is not accessible by default - add fallbacks.
pitfalls: Sizing canvas only with CSS - blurry output.
Forgetting beginPath() so old shapes redraw.
Using canvas for simple icons where SVG is better.

examples.title: Draw shapes and animate a ball
examples.html: <canvas id="c" width="320" height="160" aria-label="Bouncing ball animation" role="img"></canvas>

interview.a: A bitmap drawing surface controlled with JavaScript through a rendering context such as 2D or WebGL.
Canvas is pixel-based and fast for many objects but not scalable or DOM-accessible; SVG is vector-based, scalable and each element is in the DOM.

topics.title: Inline SVG Basics
topics.summary: SVG draws crisp, scalable vector graphics directly in HTML and can be styled with CSS.
topics.description: **SVG** (Scalable Vector Graphics) describes shapes in XML. It scales to any size without blurring, is small for icons and logos, and can be styled and scripted like HTML. ### Ways to use SVG 1. **Inline**: paste the ``** - simple, cached, not stylable from the page. 3. **CSS background** image. ### Core elements | Element | Draws | |---|---| | `` | Rectangle (x, y, width, height, rx) | | `` | cx, cy, r | | `` | cx, cy, rx, ry | | `` | x1,y1 → x2,y2 | | `` / `` | points="..." | | `` | Any shape (M, L, C, Z commands) | | `` | Text | | `` | Group | ### viewBox - the key to scaling `viewBox="0 0 100 100"` defines the internal coordinate system. With `width="100%"` the whole drawing scales to fit. ### Styling Presentation attributes (`fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`) or CSS. Use `fill="currentColor"` so icons inherit text colour. ### Accessibility Add `role="img"` plus `` inside, or `aria-hidden="true"` for decorative icons. ### Animation CSS transitions/animations, SMIL (`<animate>`) or JavaScript all work.
keyPoints: SVG is vector based: sharp at any size.
viewBox defines the coordinate system for scaling.
Inline SVG can be styled by CSS and scripted by JS.
fill="currentColor" lets icons follow the text colour.
Add title/role="img" or aria-hidden for accessibility.
pitfalls: Missing viewBox - the drawing does not scale.
Hard-coded fill colours that cannot be themed.
No alternative text on meaningful graphics.

examples.html: I love SVG

interview.a: It defines the SVG internal coordinate system (min-x, min-y, width, height) so the graphic scales to its container.
It is resolution independent, small, stylable with CSS and can inherit text colour via currentColor.

topics.title: template & slot Elements
topics.summary: template holds inert HTML to clone later; slot marks insertion points inside shadow DOM.
topics.description: ### template `
keyPoints: template content is inert until cloned.
Clone with template.content.cloneNode(true).
slot is a placeholder filled with light-DOM content.
Named slots use slot="name" on children.
Use textContent when inserting user data.
pitfalls: Expecting template content to be visible without cloning.
Using innerHTML with user input and creating XSS holes.
Forgetting cloneNode(true) so children are not copied.

examples.title: Render a list from a template

interview.a: A container for HTML that is parsed but not rendered; you clone its content with JavaScript to create elements.
It defines a placeholder in a shadow DOM component that the component user fills with their own content.

topics.title: Web Components: Custom Elements & Shadow DOM
topics.summary: Create your own reusable tags with customElements.define, shadow DOM and templates.
keyPoints: Custom element names must contain a hyphen.
attachShadow creates an encapsulated DOM and CSS scope.
Lifecycle: connectedCallback, attributeChangedCallback, disconnectedCallback.
Use slots for content projection.
Style from outside through CSS variables or ::part().
pitfalls: Custom element name without a hyphen - define() throws.
Doing DOM work in the constructor instead of connectedCallback.
Forgetting to list attributes in observedAttributes.

examples.title: A custom <user-badge> element
examples.html: This page style does not affect the badge internals.
examples.explanation: The hyphenated tag is registered once and can be reused anywhere.

interview.q: What are the main parts of Web Components?
interview.a: Custom Elements, Shadow DOM and HTML templates/slots.

interview.q: Why must custom element names contain a hyphen?
interview.a: To avoid clashes with current and future built-in HTML elements.
Encapsulation: component markup and styles are isolated from the rest of the document.
